articles.title: Dinho manda recado a ministros e políticos antes de tocar 'Que país é este' no Rock in Rio  | G1
articles.standfirst: Vocalista do Capital Inicial fez discurso antes de cantar o clássico da Legião Urbana em show que homenageou os 30 anos da morte de Renato Russo.
articles.summary: Vocalista do Capital Inicial fez discurso antes de cantar o clássico da Legião Urbana em show que homenageou os 30 anos da morte de Renato Russo.
articles.body:
O vocalista do Capital Inicial, Dinho Ouro Preto, fez um discurso com críticas a ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) e a políticos antes de cantar "Que País É Este?", clássico da Legião Urbana, durante o show da banda no Rock in Rio, na noite de sexta-feira (4). ( leia aqui a resenha crítica )

HORÁRIOS ROCK IN RIO: Confira a programação completa

"Essa próxima música aqui é para o Daniel Vorcaro, falou? Essa música aqui é para os ministros do STF, que nos devem explicações. Essa aqui é para os nossos políticos de direita, de centro e de esquerda, que nos devem explicações", afirmou o cantor.

Na sequência, Dinho disse acreditar na democracia brasileira. "A democracia brasileira vai sobreviver a isso. Nós, juntos, somos mais fortes", declarou.

Antes de iniciar a música, ele concluiu: "Isso aqui é para a distopia brasileira. Isso aqui se chama 'Que País É Este?'".

As críticas do vocalista acontecem em meio às investigação sobre supostas fraudes envolvendo o extinto Banco Master desencadeou uma das maiores crises políticas e institucionais de 2026 ao atingir o STF, a Polícia Federal, a Procuradoria-Geral da República e o Palácio do Planalto.

A divulgação de relatórios da PF pelo ministro André Mendonça expôs mensagens que apontam uma relação de proximidade entre o ministro Alexandre de Moraes e o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, levando Moraes a negar irregularidades e pedir uma investigação contra o colega. ( Entenda a crise no STF )

O show marcou o encerramento do primeiro dia do Palco Sunset e reuniu o Capital Inicial e o guitarrista Dado Villa-Lobos em uma homenagem aos 30 anos da morte de Renato Russo e à trajetória da Legião Urbana.

A apresentação reuniu sucessos das duas bandas. Do Capital Inicial, o repertório incluiu "Quatro Vezes Você", "Independência", "Música Urbana", "Fátima", "Veraneio Vascaína" e "Natasha".

Dinho Ouro Preto se apresenta com Capital Inicial e Dado Villa-Lobos no Rock in Rio — Foto: Anderson Bordê/AgNews

Em homenagem à Legião Urbana, Dinho dividiu o palco com Dado Villa-Lobos para interpretar "Será", "Geração Coca-Cola", "Quase Sem Querer", "Tempo Perdido" e "Que País É Este?".

Embora a Legião Urbana nunca tenha se apresentado no Rock in Rio com Renato Russo, o festival realizou, em 2011, um Concerto Sinfônico em homenagem à banda no Palco Mundo.

O show desta sexta-feira marcou a décima apresentação do Capital Inicial no Rock in Rio, colocando a banda entre as artistas que mais vezes participaram do festival.

articles.title: João Victor Gonçalves, de Quem Ama Cuida, denuncia homofobia no RIR | G1
articles.standfirst: João Victor Gonçalves foi seguido por GH e amigos, que fizeram comentários e debocharam de sua roupa. Após a repercussão do vídeo, o streamer pediu desculpas e disse que fazia apenas 'entretenimento' na rua.
articles.summary: João Victor Gonçalves, o Mau Mau de Quem Ama Cuida, foi seguido pelo streamer GH Rell RJ no Rock in Rio e denunciou comentários homofóbicos feitos durante live.
articles.body:
João Victor Gonçalves, que interpreta Mau Mau em “Quem Ama Cuida”, acusou o streamer GH de homofobia após ser abordado no entorno do Rock in Rio. — Foto: Globo/Bob Paulino

O ator João Victor Gonçalves, que interpreta Mau Mau na novela “Quem Ama Cuida”, acusou um streamer de homofobia após ser abordado durante o Rock in Rio, na noite desta sexta-feira (4).

O episódio aconteceu no entorno da Cidade do Rock, no Rio de Janeiro, e foi transmitido ao vivo pela plataforma Kick, concorrente da Twitch.

Na transmissão, o streamer GH Rell RJ aparece acompanhado de amigos enquanto se aproxima do ator. Em determinado momento, eles fazem comentários sobre a roupa usada por João Victor. “Caralho, que é isso. Cara horroroso. Cara meteu um tomate”, dizem.

O grupo ainda aparece seguindo o ator por alguns segundos.

O trecho da transmissão foi posteriormente recortado e publicado nas redes sociais, onde passou a circular com críticas à "abordagem". Durante a live, não fica claro se o streamer e os amigos sabiam que o homem era o artista João Victor Gonçalves.

O g1 procurou o streamer GH e a plataforma Kick para esclarecer o episódio e saber quais são as políticas em relação a abordagens e comportamentos como os registrados na transmissão. Até a última atualização desta reportagem, não houve retorno de nenhuma das partes.

Após a repercussão do vídeo, o ator se manifestou nas redes sociais e classificou o episódio como homofobia.

“Somos mais fortes que qualquer coisa... Impunes não vão ficar, homofobia é crime. Isso é um retrato. Meu medo de ser roubado era maior. Homofobia não é entretenimento”, disse emocionado.

João Victor traçou ainda um paralelo entre o que viveu e a história de seu personagem em “Quem Ama Cuida”. Na trama, Mau Mau é um jovem em processo de descoberta da própria sexualidade que enfrenta a homofobia dentro de casa, principalmente nas relações com o avô, Otoniel (Tony Ramos).

Em seus stories, o ator afirmou que o episódio no Rock in Rio era “o retrato de tudo que a gente mostra” na novela.

“O Mau Mau é um personagem forte, valente, que encara essa homofobia estrutural que vive dentro de casa de uma forma muito corajosa. Ele engole e segue”, escreveu.

GH Rell RJ também se pronunciou sobre o episódio e afirmou que costuma fazer transmissões com abordagens e situações inusitadas nas ruas.

Segundo ele, o trecho foi retirado do contexto da live e acabou gerando uma onda de críticas nas redes sociais.

“Tava numa live aqui, mano, e eu fico fazendo um monte de entretenimento no meio da rua, tipo doideira com maluquice. Tava fazendo entretenimento com um cara que tava passando na rua e me dei mal. Sabe por quê? Cliparam, postaram lá no Twitter e eu tô recebendo um monte de hate. Se eu errei, eu peço desculpas porque nós é ser humano e nós erra”, afirmou.

A repercussão também provocou manifestações de colegas de elenco de João Victor em “Quem Ama Cuida”. Pedro Alves, que interpreta Fernando na novela, publicou uma mensagem em defesa do ator.

“Aquilo foi baixo, covarde e cruel. Aquilo não é brincadeira. Só quem sofre pode entender. Vergonha de ver que falhamos como sociedade", escreveu.

Pedro Alves, colega de elenco de João Victor Gonçalves em 'Quem Ama Cuida', se manifestou em apoio ao ator após o episódio no Rock in Rio — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram/Pedro Alves

articles.title: Festival tem três noites de shows com entrada gratuita ns Capital  | G1
articles.standfirst: As apresentações ocorrem neste sábado (5), domingo (6) e segunda-feira (7), no Teatro Dom Bosco, com coral, orquestra, violoncelo, percussão e Libras.
articles.summary: As apresentações ocorrem neste sábado (5), domingo (6) e segunda-feira (7), no Teatro Dom Bosco, com coral, orquestra, violoncelo, percussão e Libras.
articles.body:
Mais de 150 alunos sobem ao palco para o festival — Foto: Divulgação

Mais de 150 alunos de diferentes regiões de Campo Grande vão subir ao palco do Teatro Dom Bosco neste fim de semana para apresentar o resultado de um projeto de formação musical gratuita. O evento terá apresentações de coral, orquestra, violoncelo, percussão e Libras.

O Festival Compondo Talentos ocorre neste sábado (5), domingo (6) e segunda-feira (7), com apresentações de coral, orquestra, violão, violoncelo, percussão e até música acompanhada por Libras. A entrada é gratuita.

As apresentações começam às 18h30 no sábado e no domingo. Na segunda-feira, o festival começa às 18h. O Teatro Dom Bosco fica na Avenida Mato Grosso, 225, no Centro de Campo Grande.

O festival marca o encerramento do ciclo de formação do projeto, que reuniu 12 turmas ligadas a escolas, instituições e projetos sociais da capital. Durante as atividades, os participantes tiveram contato com diferentes linguagens musicais, incluindo canto coral, violão, violoncelo, percussão, banda, orquestra e Libras.

A proposta é levar ao palco um trabalho desenvolvido ao longo dos meses em diferentes pontos da cidade. O presidente do Instituto Cerrado Central, Daniel Escrivano, responsável pela realização do projeto, destaca a importância da iniciativa:

“Todo talento começa com a oportunidade de experimentar, aprender e ser ouvido.”

A programação foi dividida em três noites, com grupos diferentes em cada apresentação. Confira a programação completa;

Grupo de violão durante os ensaios — Foto: Divulgação

O primeiro dia de apresentações reúne corais, orquestras e turmas que destacam a diversidade musical do projeto. Encerrando a noite, a Orquestra Indígena, desenvolvida na Aldeia Urbana Darcy Ribeiro, combina música de concerto com cantos tradicionais e elementos das culturas indígena e brasileira:

Canto coral da Escola Municipal Dr. Tertuliano Meireles

Violoncelo da Orquestra Sinfônica Municipal de Campo Grande

Orquestra Indígena, da Fundação Ueze Zahran

A programação do segundo dia traz uma mistura de vozes, inclusão e ritmos afro-brasileiros, destacando a transformação social por meio da arte:

Canto coral do Lar do Pequeno Assis e da Associação Escola de Mãe Luz, com uma apresentação que integra a Língua Brasileira de Sinais (Libras) ao canto

Grupo de percussão Bojomalê, com uma performance marcada por percussão corporal, ritmos afro-brasileiros e maracatu

Orquestra Fraternidade Sem Fronteiras, projeto que oferece formação musical gratuita para crianças e adolescentes de 7 a 17 anos em situação de vulnerabilidade

No feriado da Independência, o encerramento do festival celebra a união de diferentes instrumentos, vozes e talentos da região:

Grupo de violão da Igreja Batista Popular

Grupo de música do Instituto Misericórdia

Projeto Madeiras Dedilhadas, da Universidade Federal de Mato Grosso do Sul (UFMS), responsável pelo show de encerramento

O festival é o resultado de um projeto de formação musical gratuita — Foto: Divulgação

Horário: 18h30 nos dias 5 e 6; 18h no dia 7

Local: Teatro Dom Bosco – Avenida Mato Grosso, 225, Centro, Campo Grande

articles.title: Dolly Parton’s sister reacts to ‘insensitivity’ from strangers after the ‘Jolene' singer passed away
articles.summary: Stella Parton expresses the family's grief over Dolly Parton's death, addressing insensitivity from strangers and calling for compassion and respect in her remembrance.
articles.body: Dolly Parton’s sister, Stella Parton, opened up about how the family has been dealing with the singer’s demise. She also warned everyone against making inconsiderate comments. Sharing that she has faced a lot of “insensitivity from strangers” after her sister left for her heavenly abode, Stella detailed how the Parton family is taking on all of the challenges altogether.Stella Parton opens up about how she has been dealing with things after Dolly Parton’s demiseThe 77-year-old singer-songwriter recently shared an Instagram post detailing how many people posted insensitive comments after her sister, Dolly Parton's, passed away. She expressed her gratitude for the people who have been wishing well for the family and actually showed up.She wrote, “First let me say, thank you to the ones of you who have shown ‘genuine’ support and love during this time of our family bereavement. We will be okay in time, but each of us will grieve in our own personal way. Every human being experiences pain and loss in life, and my family is no different.”She further added, “Sadly, because of the way our lives have been lived in front of the public, we have no choice but to be subjected to incredible pressure and insensitivity from strangers.”Stella Parton asks people to make a change in their lives and get inspired by Dolly PartonFurther down the post, she finally shared that people need to learn some compassion in their everyday life. She wrote. “Finally, I ask that you show more compassion and wisdom as we move forward in life. Use my sister’s life as an example for tolerance and respect toward others. It’s not about the most clever comments, fake AI garbage, or snarky tweets.”She concluded her post by adding, “That being said, I’ve always embraced my own personality and will continue to be myself and express my opinions as I deem appropriate regardless of what anyone thinks of me. It’s my right as a human being! Have a happy and safe weekend.”Dolly Parton passed away on August 25 after battling cancer. The singer had not revealed her health issues until after her passing. A statement from her representatives shared with PEOPLE revealed that the iconic star had left for her heavenly abode while she was admitted to a cancer facility, surrounded by family and loved ones. Her nephew, Bryan Seaver, was one of the first ones to inform everyone about Parton’s demise, sharing a video on all of her accounts.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Taapsee Pannu CALLS OUT Bollywood's obsession with 'same actors': 'All the rom-coms, glam stuff looks the same'
articles.summary: Taapsee Pannu has never shied away from calling out patterns she sees in the film industry. In her latest chat, she took aim at something many viewers.
articles.body: Taapsee Pannu has never shied away from calling out patterns she sees in the film industry. In her latest chat, she took aim at something many viewers have quietly noticed too: Bollywood films starting to feel repetitive because the same faces keep showing up in the same kind of stories. The actor, known for choosing offbeat and gritty roles, spoke candidly about how typecasting isn't just an actor's problem but a casting problem that filmmakers need to fix.Same actors, same genres, says Taapsee PannuSpeaking to Hindustan Times, Taapsee Pannu pointed out that Bollywood keeps recycling a small pool of actors for particular genres, which she believes is the real reason so many films end up looking alike. According to her, when studios rely on the same handful of stars for romance or glamour and another fixed set for thrillers, originality naturally takes a hit.She explained, "All the rom-coms, glam stuff looks the same because there are only those four or five actors, actresses who are doing that. All our thrillers look and feel the same because there are only those four or five actors who are doing that."She added that true novelty on screen requires filmmakers to be bolder with their choices. She said, "If you really want your film to look different, something new, something different, then you need to cast people who can bring that difference on screen."Costume changes don't erase the old image, says Taapsee PannuTaapsee Pannu also touched on how simply changing an actor's look or outfit doesn't automatically make a role feel fresh, since audiences already carry a fixed impression of that performer. She said, "If I've seen someone in a glamorous role, now you make that person wear a sari or a bikini or whatever, I have seen the glamour of that actor. It's only different, right?” she said, adding, “So that's not the fault of that poor actor, also."Taapsee Pannu on being typecast herselfTurning to her own journey, Taapsee Pannu acknowledged that she too has become synonymous with intense, hard-hitting characters, largely because those are the scripts she keeps receiving. She reasoned that picking the strongest script from a limited set only reinforces the label further. She said, "If you only offer me 10 intense films, I will choose the best out of them and present that, but it will still be a strong woman, intense film because that's the only genre that people have started imagining me."More about Taapsee Pannu's upcoming film 'Gandhari'Taapsee's remarks come alongside the release of her latest film, 'Gandhari', directed by Devashish Makhija and written and produced by Kanika Dhillon. She plays Bani, a mother whose life turns upside down after her daughter is kidnapped, pushing her into the eerie town of Joypurra and its unsettling Behrupiya lore. Ishwak Singh, Jatin Sarna, Swastika Mukherjee, Mita Vashisht, and Chhaya Kadam also star. The film began streaming on Netflix on September 3.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: VHP bars Muslims from garba, dandiya events in Maharashtra; issues Aadhaar, tilak guidelines
articles.summary: MUMBAI: The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) has said Muslims will not be allowed to participate in garba and dandiya events across Maharashtra during next.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) has said Muslims will not be allowed to participate in garba and dandiya events across Maharashtra during next month’s Navratri festival and has issued guidelines asking organisers to verify participants’ Hindu identity.The measures suggested by the organisation include checking Aadhaar cards and applying tilak on the foreheads of attendees when Navratri begins on October 11.VHP spokesperson and joint secretary Shriraj Nair said the organisation had decided to prevent Muslims from taking part in garba and dandiya events during the festival, news agency PTI reported."We have taken a decision of not allowing participation of Muslims in garba-dandiya dance during the Navratri festival," Nair said."Navratri is not just about songs and dance. The festival is about worshipping the Goddess. Why should Muslims, who are against idol worship, participate in the festival?" he said.VHP issues guidelines for garba, dandiya organisersThe VHP has also issued guidelines for organisers, including checking Aadhaar cards of attendees and applying tilak as measures to verify their Hindu identity.Nair said the restrictions were not aimed at any particular community and described them as precautionary steps intended to preserve what the organisation considers the cultural character of Hindu festivals."The VHP, which is unwilling to compromise on its core agenda of religious conversion and anti-cow slaughter, believes festivals are an integral part of the cultural legacy of the Hindus. And it cannot allow its dilution. However, it admits the restrictions are precautionary measures and not directed against Muslims or any other communities," he said.VHP refuses to comment on Bhagwat remarksNair’s remarks came days after RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, while addressing a gathering at Madison Square in New York, spoke about universal oneness and dignity for all people."If any Hindu thinks there should be no Muslims in India, he will not remain Hindu. If you want to call yourself a Hindu, you have to believe that all paths are leading to the same goal. Every human has dignity. There is no difference between human beings," Bhagwat had said.Asked about Bhagwat’s remarks, Nair said the VHP would not comment on the RSS chief’s statement."We are not against anybody. We also believe in social harmony and peace," he said.Nair, however, questioned why the VHP should ease its guidelines for Muslims whom he said did not subscribe to the religious beliefs and form of worship associated with Navratri."The point is, why should we relax our guidelines for Muslims who don't subscribe to our religious beliefs and style of worship?" he said."If Muslims are keen to participate in the Navratri festivities, they should come with their family members, wives and sisters. They should organise the Navratri festivals in the mosques or places of their residences," Nair said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: 'Mirzapur: The Movie' box office collection Day 2 [LIVE]: Pankaj Tripathi, Ravi Kishan, and Ali Fazal starrer is set to cross Rs 45 crore on second day
articles.summary: 'Mirzapur: The Movie' has hit theatres this Friday and has been earning good reviews, and the same is reflected in its box office. Starring Pankaj Tri.
articles.body: 'Mirzapur: The Movie' has hit theatres this Friday and has been earning good reviews, and the same is reflected in its box office. Starring Pankaj Tripathi, Ali Fazal and Ravi Kishan in lead roles, the film has made a strong start at the domestic box office. Here's how it is performing on Day 2 at the box office.'Mirzapur: The Movie' box office collection Day 2 [LIVE]The Gurmeet Singh directorial opened to massive box office numbers. The film raked in Rs 25.75 crore across 11,135 shows on Day 1. Now, according to the Sacnilk report, on Day 2, the movie is currently running across 8,112 shows. As of now, the big-screen adaptation of the 'Mirzapur' web show has earned Rs 12.80 crore on Day 2. The numbers are expected to increase as the day progresses.With that, the total India gross collection has reached Rs 46 crore, while the total India net collection is now Rs 38.55 crore. The final box office numbers for the day are yet to be reported.Mirzapur: The Movie ReviewBox office competition'Mirzapur: The Movie' is currently competing against Yash-starrer 'Toxic: A Fairytale for Grown Ups' and the movie that is growing every passing day, 'Hanuman Ansh', at the box office. Meanwhile, the Pankaj Tripathi starrer is also sharing screens with Arshad Warsi's 'Jeevan Bheema Yojana'.More about 'Mirzapur: The Movie'The theatrical adaptation brings several changes to the cast, with Jitendra Kumar stepping into the role of Bablu Pandit, earlier played by Vikrant Massey. Ravi Kishan also joins the cast, bringing a fresh presence to the story.However, the film keeps the essence of the original intact. Actors Abhishek Banerjee, Rasika Dugal, Sheeba Chadha, Rajesh Tailang, Shriya Pilgaonkar, Harshita Shekhar Gaur and Shweta Tripathi return to their respective roles. Along with them, Pankaj Tripathi, Ali Fazal and Divyenndu reprise their key characters, bringing the familiar world of the series to the big screen.The film was released in theatres on September 4, 2026.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Robotaxis enter their villain era
articles.summary: Road Rage is a new short film in production that casts a murderous autonomous car as the bad guy — and taps into everything people already fear about AI on the road.
articles.body: It’s Bullitt meets Christine meets Waymo. A new short film imagines a San Francisco car chase where the other driver isn’t human — and the car may be trying to kill you. That a robotaxi can now be cast as the villain with almost no explanation says something about the present moment. Autonomous cars have gone from sci-fi curiosities to fixtures in some American cities, where they’ve become stand-ins for anxieties about AI job displacement, Big Tech surveillance, and machines making decisions once left to humans. Road Rage, the planned short film awaiting $40,000 on Kickstarter to fund production, leans into all of it. The film pits Joa, a ridehail driver in a manual-transmission car, against Roboride, an autonomous vehicle that takes a minor road-rage incident very personally, according to a synopsis by its director, Romain Thomassin. Roboride lightly clips Joa’s mirror. Joa gives it the finger. The car decides to kill him. “It’s analog versus artificial,” Thomassin told The Verge. [Media: The AI bad guy will be played by an old Prius transformed with cold LED lights across the front — à la Tesla — fake cameras, a spinning lidar-like device on the roof, a black exterior, and a menacing, ever-blinking red dot. Thomassin calls the intended result a “nasty Waymo.” “I really wanted to play the nasty, gritty look of the ’70s car chase, but with today’s robotaxi in today’s San Francisco,” he said. The chase itself will be a throwback: real cars, real actors, and real stunts. "“I really wanted to play the nasty, gritty look of the ’70s car chase, but with today’s robotaxi in today’s San Francisco.”" - Road Rage director Romain Thomassin “What makes Joa the good guy is not only his instinct but also his authenticity,” Thomassin said, noting a scene in which the character has an unexpected conversation with his passengers. “This type of human interaction doesn’t happen in a robotaxi.” Thomassin doesn’t actually think robotaxis are inherently evil. But as a movie villain, they come preloaded with tension. For one thing, they’re replacing the kind of worker his protagonist represents. Joa is a Mexican immigrant trying to make a living driving in an increasingly expensive San Francisco. Robotaxis are already competing with ridehail drivers, just as generative AI is competing with workers in Thomassin’s own industry. “Driving here is a metaphor for what’s happening in cinema, in filmmaking,” Thomassin said. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Then there’s surveillance. Autonomous cars are covered in cameras and sensors, constantly observing the streets — and people — around them. That, more than the prospect of being driven around without a human behind the wheel, is what actually unnerves Thomassin. In Road Rage, that anxiety is pushed toward dystopia. There’s a brief encounter involving immigration enforcement, and Thomassin imagines a feature-length version in which autonomous cars identify people, trap passengers inside, or deliver them directly to authorities. The progression, as he describes it, is observation, surveillance, then control. “The next step is that [autonomous vehicles] could become the police,” he said. And because robotaxis operate as connected fleets, the threat can scale beyond one vehicle. “Imagine an army rising up,” Thomassin said. Robotaxis also make unusually good revenge-movie villains because people already treat them like adversaries. Thomassin points to the indignities Waymos have endured on San Francisco streets: people immobilizing them with traffic cones, tagging and vandalizing them, and even setting them on fire. “They are being bullied,” he said. In Road Rage, that mistreatment becomes the motivation: “They want to take revenge.” Thomassin describes Roboride as absorbing the behavior it observes around it — including the behavior of human drivers. The car is simply learning road rage from humans. “Humans are known to be the worst versions of themselves on the road,” he said. That makes Roboride a very 2026 update to the killer car idea in Stephen King’s Christine. There, the menace is supernatural. Here, it comes from something more contemporary: a machine that watches humans, learns from them, and inherits some of their worst traits along with the useful ones. On the other side of the chase is Joa and his stick shift — a deliberately analog counterpoint. To Thomassin, driving stick is a deeply human act: The driver remains in control of the vehicle, physically responding to the road. What separates Joa from Roboride, in Thomassin’s telling, is instinct — and even irrationality. During one confrontation, Joa takes his hands off the steering wheel while facing down the autonomous car. The move is so reckless that Roboride backs off. The human wins by becoming less predictable than the machine. "“Respect your madness. Be a little mad and creative in your way of doing things, and you will be able to rise against the machines.”" - Romain Thomassin “Respect your madness,” Thomassin said. “Be a little mad and creative in your way of doing things, and you will be able to rise against the machines.” Despite its skepticism toward AI, Road Rage may use some of the technology itself. Thomassin says the filmmakers are considering AI-generated imagery to depict what Roboride sees, while shooting the human driver’s world with traditional cinematography. To him, that distinction matters. He sees AI as a creative tool when it serves the story, rather than simply a way to replace workers. For all the menace he sees in robotaxis, Thomassin isn’t afraid to ride in them. He signed up for Waymo as soon as he could and uses it when visiting friends and family for rides. “I don’t feel in danger,” he said. That may be what makes Roboride such an effective 2026 villain. The scary part isn’t necessarily that the machine will crash. The scary part is that the machine works.

articles.title: Prince Harry, Meghan Markle accused of seeking ‘best of both worlds’ with UK move: expert
articles.summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's U.K. return mirrors the "half-in half-out" arrangement Queen Elizabeth rejected, a royal expert says.
articles.body: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have returned to the United Kingdom with their two children, but royal experts say the move may be less about a permanent homecoming and more about securing the "best of both worlds." The Duke and Duchess of Sussex — who are reportedly looking for a home in Britain — are expected to maintain their ties to Montecito, California, while keeping their businesses based in the United States. Royal commentator Kinsey Schofield told Fox News Digital that the reported arrangement appears to give the couple access to Britain and the royal family while allowing them to maintain their independent lives in the U.S. "I suspect they want the best of both worlds — access to Britain, proximity to the monarchy and the credibility that comes with Harry’s royal identity, while maintaining the freedom and commercial opportunities they associate with life outside the U.K.," Schofield said. PRINCE WILLIAM, KATE MIDDLETON FACE 'SUSSEX CIRCUS' AS PRINCE GEORGE PREPARES FOR ETON: EXPERT Schofield said the Sussexes’ reported plans resemble the "half-in, half-out" role that Queen Elizabeth II rejected when Harry and Meghan stepped back from royal duties in 2020. MEGHAN MARKLE’S UK RETURN POSES PALACE CONTROL ‘NIGHTMARE,’ EXPERT WARNS While the couple has reportedly vowed to avoid making public comments or releasing photos that could overshadow Prince George's start at Eton this month, Schofield said the Sussexes’ broader U.K. plans raise questions about whether they are truly returning to Britain for good or simply testing the waters. "Harry and Meghan never do what they say or say what they mean," she said. "One year ago, Harry told us the U.K. was not safe enough to bring his wife and children. Now someone is briefing the Daily Mail that Harry has a 15-year plan in the U.K. Alternatively, we’re briefed this could be temporary." "I would describe it as a trial run rather than a definitive homecoming," Schofield added. Harry and Meghan relocated to California in 2020 after stepping back as working members of the royal family. Since then, they have released various projects, including a Netflix docuseries and Harry’s memoir, "Spare," and have pursued a series of entertainment and business ventures outside the monarchy. However, their return to Britain has raised questions about their motives. Royal commentator Richard Fitzwilliams said Harry and Meghan have increasingly presented themselves as an "international" power couple, rather than tying themselves to either the U.K. or the U.S. PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE'S UK RETURN SIGNALS ‘SPECTACULAR DEFEAT’ AS ROYAL EXPERTS WARN OF WILLIAM SHOWDOWN "They reportedly see themselves as ‘international citizens,’" Fitzwilliams told Fox News Digital. "They claim that their balance of business activities and trips abroad over the last six years is a success." WATCH: PRINCE HARRY BELIEVED ROYAL FAMILY COULD HAVE ALLOWED A ‘HYBRID’ ROLE: AUTHOR "Rather than planting one flag, the Sussexes appear to be keeping several doors open," Schofield added. Helena Chard, a British broadcaster and photographer, also said Harry and Meghan are "keeping their options open." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "Things haven’t gone to plan for various reasons, but one thing’s for sure: They need to keep relevant," Chard told Fox News Digital. "Cue travel to the U.K., be seen with the British Royal Family and push for state-funded armed police protection." Chard said enrolling the children in a British school could benefit the family while also helping Harry pursue the security arrangements he has sought since stepping back as a working royal. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS WATCH: PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE RETURNING TO THE UK: 'GOD HELP THE ROYAL FAMILY' "Like a dog with a bone, Harry will fight for everything he believes his family deserves," Chard said. The experts also questioned whether Harry and Meghan are equally invested in making Britain a permanent home. "Harry has much more at stake emotionally," Schofield said. "Returning gives him an opportunity to reconnect with his country, his family, old friends and a version of his identity that he walked away from six years ago." PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE "For Meghan, Britain carries different associations," she continued. "She has repeatedly described her royal experience as deeply unhappy, so I think it is reasonable to question whether she could ever feel the same enthusiasm Harry might feel about putting down permanent roots." "Harry may see Britain as coming home. Meghan may see Britain as somewhere useful to spend part of the year," Schofield said. "Those are two very different emotional investments." articles.title: Parmish Verma confirms his DIVORCE and new relationship as he slams online trolls; says it is manhood ‘to respect my ex-wife, and the woman in my life today’
articles.summary: Parmish Verma confirms his divorce from Geet Grewal and addresses online trolls, emphasizing the importance of respecting his ex-wife and current partner. Discover his thoughts on masculinity and public perception.
articles.body: Punjabi singer Parmish Verma has been ruling social media for quite some time now. Usually that happens because of his music, a virtual home tour or his upcoming projects. However, this time, things are a tad different. He was all over the internet for his rumoured relationship with Harman Brar and for allegedly cheating on his wife Geet Grewal. He was receiving heavy criticism for his posts with Harman, and finally, the ‘Gal Ni Kadni’ artist, Parmish Verma, has addressed the trolling head-on. He slammed the online trolls and confirmed being divorced. He also confessed to being in a relationship.About Parmish Verma and Harman BrarThe romantic videos of Parmish Verma and Harman Brar sparked online buzz recently. While many thought it was just a marketing stunt for an upcoming song, several others called Parmish Verma a red flag for cheating on his wife with Harman. Later, on Harman’s birthday, when Parmish Verma addressed her as ‘love,’ the speculations reached new heights.Parmish Verma confirms his divorce and breaks silence of on relationship rumoursTaking to his social media handle, Parmish Verma shared a long note. He first of all said that people are calling him a cheater simply becuase of a preassumed notion that a men has to be the villian in a failed relationship.He wrote, “Being a man makes you a convenient psychological scapegoat; blame the gender, simplify the story, and the mob gets to feel morally superior. I understand the psychology of it, and I accept the burden without resentment.”Addressing his hard times in a now-expired Instagram story, Parmish added, “When I was drowning, nobody came to save me. I dealt with my own consequences, carried my own pain, and learned to stand again. That, too, is being a man.”Further, confirming his relationship status, Parmish wrote, “So is having the discipline to respect my ex-wife, respect the woman in my life today, and never confuse bitterness with masculinity.”“What isn't manhood is weakness disguised as virtue, becoming a weasel in a mob, feeding an agenda for attention and money and calling cowardice morality. I know what I am. I would rather be hated for standing upright than applauded for crawling with the crowd. I'm proud of the man I became,” he concluded.About Parmish Verma and his ex-wife Geet GrewalParmish Verma and Geet Grewal got married in October 2021. They were in a relationship for a long time, and then exchanged vows in a big fat Indian wedding. There was no phone policy at their wedding, which left Parmish's friend and Punjabi artist Sharry Mann furious. The matter was escalated to a level where heated words were exchanged. In 2022, they welcomed their firstborn, Sadaa. Parmish announced the news of Sadaa's birth with pure joy. Fast forward to 2026, in January, a document went viral on social media, which alleged that Parmish and Geet parted ways. Both parties maintained silence over the matter until Parmish’s latest post.Give your child the gift of confidence! Claim your exclusive TOI Masterclass spot today!

articles.title: De Hannah Montana, pasando por Miley Cyrus y ahora vuelve a modificar su nombre artístico
articles.standfirst: La artista decide llamarse simplemente Miley, elimina Cyrus y su padre reacciona a ello
articles.summary: La artista decide llamarse simplemente Miley, elimina Cyrus y su padre reacciona a ello
articles.body: Miley Cyrus anunció por sorpresa su nuevo álbum, cuyo título lleva 'Bass Persuades', y saldrá a la luz el próximo 18 de septiembre. Lo presentará en dos conciertos en el Hollywood Bowl durante el mes de octubre, algo que supone su vuelta a los escenarios tras años alejada de ellos. Pero este nuevo anuncio ha dejado un detalle curioso que no ha pasado inadvertido. Su nombre. Más en concreto. Su nuevo nombre. La estrella de Disney se ha quitado su apellido, para simplemente pasar a llamarse Miley. Y lo ha hecho por una razón familiar. De los primeros que han reaccionado a esta maniobra de la artista ha sido precisamente su padre, Billy Ray Cyrus, que ha reaccionado al respecto en sus redes sociales. "La familia significa más que nunca ahora. Siempre llamé a mi pequeña Miley. Simplemente... Miley. Igual que siempre llamé a mi hijito Braison", comenzó el artista de country en su texto. "Apuesto a que no lo sabías… Yo era simplemente Cyrus antes de que saliera Achy Breaky Heart en el 92. Toda mi ropa y camisetas solo decían: 'Cyruslo dio todo' con una imagen de una bandera de POWMIA y la frase: 'No te olvidamos", añadía su padre. De hecho, su padre reaccionaba con naturalidad a tal efecto. "Ayer le dije a Miley que me parecía bien que usara su nombre de pila. Mencioné a Dolly y Cher. Lo pienso cada vez más… Elvis… Prince… y así sucesivamente. Es una progresión natural para una leyenda superestrella icónica". Billy Ray eludió que haya polémica con el tema en cuestión, dejando claro que no hay tensión entre ellos, ya que hace años estuvieron distanciados por la tensa separación de este con Tish, madre de la cantante, en 2022 y las dinámicas familiares acumuladas desde la época de Hannah Montana. El paso de Hannah Montana a Miley Cyrus fue una transformación profunda y rebelde con la que la artista dejó atrás su etapa en Disney Channel para construir su propia identidad musical y personal. Un cambio radical. Su momento. de la infancia a la juventud. Nuevos ritmos. Nuevos objetivos. Miley protagonizó la exitosa serie de Disney Channel durante cuatro temporadas entre 2006 y 2011. Si bien el personaje utilizaba su nombre real y mezclaba la realidad con la ficción como estrategia comercial, la cantante sentía que su imagen aniñada le había sido impuesta y necesitaba conocerse a sí misma. De ahí ese primer cambio. Y ahora llega el siguiente paso en esa fase que entiende la artista alusivo a su evolución en la vida.

articles.title: 7-year-old dies after brick column collapses  during Dahi Handi celebartion in Mumbai
articles.summary: MUMBAI: A seven-year-old boy died after a brick column collapsed on him during a local Dahi Handi celebration in Malad West on Saturday afternoon, off.
articles.body: MUMBAI: A seven-year-old boy died after a brick column collapsed on him during a local Dahi Handi celebration in Malad West on Saturday afternoon, officials said.The incident was reported around 3.01pm at Ekta Welfare Society in Chikuwadi, Malvani, where a group of children were celebrating Dahi Handi on their own.According to civic officials, the rope used for the celebration had been tied to a tree and a brick column supporting a ground-floor structure.While the children were attempting to break the handi, the column gave way and fell on the boy, identified as Rudra Kadam, 7, causing a serious head injury.The injured child was immediately rushed to Malvani General Hospital for treatment.However, hospital authorities later informed officials that Rudra was declared brought dead.Ward staff and police were mobilised after the incident.The incident occurred at Room No. 23, Ekta Welfare Society, Chikuwadi, Malvani, Marve Road, Malad West.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Box Office Comeback: How Summer 2026 offers a glimmer of hope for Hollywood in the post-COVID era
articles.summary: The summer box office has generated over $4.5 billion, with "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" and "The Odyssey" shattering records at movie theaters.
articles.body: For much of the post-COVID era, it has been an uncertain time for Hollywood and movie theaters, but this summer offers a glimmer of hope for the entertainment industry. "I have to admit going into 2026, I didn't think that the theatrical model would rebound the way it has," film critic and podcast host Christian Toto told Fox News Digital. "We're seeing some of the summer movies just really overperforming in a dramatic way." The movie box office has generated over $4.5 billion this summer according to Box Office Mojo, the highest gross since 2019. 'THE DOG STARS' REVIEW: JACOB ELORDI FIGHTS FOR SURVIVAL IN RIDLEY SCOTT'S DULL POST-APOCALYPTIC WESTERN Blockbuster hits have been shattering records. "Spider-Man: Brand New Day," which continues to dominate at the box office grossing more than $860 million domestically and over $2.2 billion globally, has become the second-highest domestic grosser of all time and third-highest globally, while Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey," has grossed more than $1.5 billion globally and is now the highest-grossing R-rated film of all time. Rotten Tomatoes box office columnist Erik Childress said the summer box office was packed with "everything," including original movies, small-budget features shattering expectations and top grossers like "Spider-Man." ‘MUTINY’ REVIEW: JASON STATHAM TAKES NO PRISONERS IN MINDLESS BUT AMUSING BRAWLER FLICK ON THE HIGH SEAS "There will always be sequels and franchises to lean on but theaters are filling up with people who want to see movies. We already have almost as many $100 million grossers (18) as we did last year (20) and there is likely another seven more in waiting this year to have the most we've seen since the pandemic and streaming gave everyone the Chicken Littles in their attitude toward the theatrical experience dying," Childress told Fox News Digital. "The box office is going to hit $9 billion for the first time since 2019 and maybe even get to the lauded $10 billion the industry has been chasing since before COVID hit." In addition to tentpole movies, low-budget horror films from young YouTubers have also defied gravity at the box office. Curry Barker's "Obsession," which defied odds by increasing its weekend grosses for multiple weeks, cracked over $500 million at the global box office, outpacing "The Mandalorian and Grogu," the latest big-budget "Star Wars" entry. And Kane Parsons' "Backrooms," made for a modest $10 million, grossed more than $81 million its opening weekend and went on to gross $390 million globally. ‘THE END OF OAK STREET’ REVIEW: ANNE HATHAWAY, EWAN MCGREGOR FIGHT DINOSAURS IN SURPRISINGLY FUN MOVIE Toto said movies like "Obsession" caught everyone off-guard. "It somehow connected with a younger audience and in a way that made them want to come back for more. It made them tell their friends. And I think that film was just really the sensation of the summer," Toto told Fox News Digital. The Hollywood in Toto founder said he's been encouraged by the box office results but stressed that Hollywood needs to continue the momentum by producing "compelling entertainment." "I think what this summer has shown is that if you put really compelling content out there, people will come," Toto said. "We love the 'Toy Story' movies, but you've got to put out an 'Obsession' now and then. You've got to put out something that people haven't seen before that says, 'Well, this speaks to me and my generation.' That matters." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

articles.title: Content creators drop the ball
articles.summary: Disruptions at the US Open and a controversial golf club ad are highlighting how influencers can be a liability for brands.
articles.body: During Naomi Osaka’s match against Anastasia Zakharova at this year’s US Open earlier this week, a gaggle of ring light-wielding influencers who were packed in a luxury suite became enough of a distraction that the umpire paused the match and repeatedly asked them to quiet down. Elsewhere in the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, other creators could be seen asking US Open staffers to take full-flash photos of them while Osaka and Zakharova were playing. Last month, United States Tennis Association (USTA) media operations director Jeanmarie Daly said that the US Open was “almost doubling” the number of content creators it was approving for credentials. There were “close to 100” influencers at this year’s tournament — up from 54 last year. But in a statement to ABC News, USTA spokesperson Brendan McIntyre emphasized that the influencers whose antics disrupted Osaka and Zakharova’s match were not credentialed by the organization. McIntyre also told The Athletic that media credentials were not given to Meg Radice and Audrey Jongens — two lifestyle influencers whose access to the US Open was revoked after they posted images of their badges to Instagram. According to McIntyre, Radice and Jongens “were improperly submitted for credentials on a staff list provided by a food vendor,” and seems like the creators might have screwed themselves over by flexing for their followers. Though those creators weren’t exactly practicing proper US Open etiquette, they were doing their jobs (read: making content) with the single-minded focus that often makes their presence an annoyance to the people around them. These influencers were at the US Open to share the experience with their followers, and regardless of whether they were invited by the USTA directly or not, they were helping the organization advertise the event to an audience that might not have otherwise been paying attention. [Media: Influencers have become an integral part of the advertising industry, with US creator ad spend hitting $37 billion in 2025 and being projected to reach $44 billion by the end of this year. Companies are increasingly relying on content creators to market their products, but what happened at the US Open is a snapshot of how that reliance can lead to undesirable outcomes for everyone involved. Videos of the US Open disruptions have gone viral across social media and sparked a conversation about whether influencers are the best people to invite to exclusive functions. But the point many people seem to be glossing over is that influencers are usually only invited to events like the US Open, awards shows, and film premieres because a brand decided it was worth bringing them there. As irksome as creators can be when they take up too much public space, that kind of behavior is something the companies that hire them have to anticipate. And as reporter Jessica Schiffer notes, some brands have been scrambling to get ahead of any potential blowback by sending out “helpful reminders” on tennis etiquette. [Media: Before a rule change in 2024, the US Open was actually much more strict about requiring attendees to stay in their seats until breaks during the match when players switch sides of the court. Now attendees can get up whenever they want, and the event features designated spaces close to the tennis courts where people can move freely — something tournament director Stacey Allaster described as “an important addition to the fan experience at the US Open.“ The influencers at this year’s US Open might not have technically been breaking any rules, but they were having a negative impact on other attendees’ viewing experience. And in the days after videos of the influencers began spreading online, the USTA put up new signage outside stadiums asking spectators to “please refrain from using flash photography or other lighting.” Taking selfies and shooting videos are core elements of the content creation hustle, but brands working with influencers should have made clear that, during a tennis tournament, there are times when it’s best to just watch the matches. While the content creators might have been having fun, many of the people around them weren’t able to enjoy the match in peace. That kind of main character energy often is exactly what companies want because it’s what keeps influencers’ fans engaged. But brands have to understand that simply letting creators run wild isn’t always the best plan of action. Callaway Golf Company learned this the hard way last month after an ad produced by YouTube channel-turned-sports apparel company Good Good hit the internet and immediately sparked outrage. The video — a spoof of Curry Barker’s Obsession — features Good Good cofounder Garrett Clark grinning maniacally after shoving professional golfer Alexis Miestowski to the ground when she reaches for his Callaway-branded driver. Many saw the ad as being distasteful and making light of violence against women, which prompted Callaway to issue an apology and sever ties with Good Good. [Media: In a statement about the ad and subsequent backlash, Callaway CEO Chip Brewer said that “mistakes were made, and we are taking the matter very seriously.” Brewer also admitted that Callaway signed off on the video before it was posted, but he insisted that its content did not reflect the company’s values. Though Callaway was quick to take the ad down, the fact that it was approved in the first place is an issue in and of itself. Even if the ad hadn’t been misogynistic, it still wasn’t funny or a particularly good riff on Obsession, and a more responsible advertising head probably would have requested significant revisions. The video was very on-brand for Good Good — a company that targets the kind of young, bro-y men whose attention (and money) the golfing industry is very keen on capturing. As The Athletic points out, Good Good is just one of many influencer outfits, including Barstool Sports and No Laying Up, that have built successful partnerships with golf brands. Similar to the way that the brands who sent influencers to the US Open should have given them some behavioral direction, companies like Callaway have to be mindful about what it means to use “edgy” content creators as their ambassadors. Influencers who have built successful platforms tend to like having creative control over the content they make, but companies paying them for promotion have a personal responsibility to make sure that they’re not being represented by people acting foolishly.

articles.title: JD Vance's mother Beverly Vance addresses 'Hillbilly Elegy' movie pay and if a sequel is possible
articles.summary: Beverly Vance says she refused to accept Hollywood's lowball offer for the "Hillbilly Elegy" film rights, revealing she's happy with her final payout.
articles.body: Beverly Vance, mother of Vice President J.D. Vance, said she was satisfied with her ultimate payout for the 2020 film adaptation of "Hillbilly Elegy," despite initial attempts by studio executives to lowball her. Appearing on OutKick’s "Tomi Lahren is Fearless," Beverly Vance addressed the business negotiations surrounding the Netflix movie based on her son’s 2016 bestselling memoir. The film featured a stacked cast, including Amy Adams portraying Beverly Vance and Glenn Close playing her mother. VANCE’S MOM FIRES BACK AT EL-SAYED OVER SECOND FAMILY JABS: ‘PROBABLY PUNCH HIM’ "Do you think that you made enough money off of 'Hillbilly Elegy'?" host Tomi Lahren asked. "I know originally they wanted to lowball you." "Um, I'm happy with what I made," Beverly Vance said. Lahren pressed further on Hollywood’s standard negotiation tactics, noting that studios often attempt to shortchange individuals selling their life rights. Vance confirmed executives initially tried to pay her less, but acknowledged she refused to accept a low offer. VANCE UNLOADS ON EL-SAYED AFTER USHA SWIPE WITH BRUTAL WARNING: 'WAY OUT OF YOUR LEAGUE' "Do you think they thought that you were just gonna just take a little amount and be fine with that? And that wasn't gonna fly with you," Lahren said, pointing out the star power attached to the project. The discussion also turned to whether the family's story could return to the screen following J.D. Vance's rise to the vice presidency. When Lahren asked if there should be a "Hillbilly Elegy 2," Vance deferred to her son. "I think that should probably be J.D.'s decision, since he wrote the book and it's based on his life," Vance said. "That would probably be his call, but whatever he decides, I would be okay with." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP For Beverly Vance, a sequel would offer an opportunity to highlight her long-term recovery following the personal addiction struggles depicted in the original movie. articles.title: Serie A official line-ups: Inter vs. Napoli
articles.summary: Inter do not give John Stones his first start behind Lautaro Martinez and Francesco Pio Esposito, as Napoli look to Rasmus Hojlund and Antonio Vergara after...
articles.body:
Inter do not give John Stones his first start behind Lautaro Martinez and Francesco Pio Esposito, as Napoli look to Rasmus Hojlund and Antonio Vergara after losing Scott McTominay.

It kicks off at San Siro at 17.00 UK time (18.00 CEST).

MILAN, ITALY – JANUARY 11: Rasmus Hojlund of SSC Napoli heads the ball whilst under pressure from from Hakan Calhanoglu of FC Internazionale Milano during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and SSC Napoli at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on January 11, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

This was the Scudetto showdown for the last two seasons, with Napoli taking the title in 2025 and Inter last term, and both are also gearing up for the start of the Champions League.

The Nerazzurri won both Serie A tests so far with Monza and Cagliari, and are taking their time to break in some summer signings.

Andy Diouf is preferred to Luis Henrique, as Djed Spence is still working his way back to full fitness, with Curtis Jones on the bench.

Lautaro Martinez and Pio Esposito are the front two again, as Marcus Thuram is not at 100 per cent.

It was reported that John Stones would get his first start in defence, but instead he is rested, along with Hakan Calhanoglu.

MILAN, ITALY – APRIL 05: Lautaro Martinez of Inter celebrates scoring his team's first goal during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and AS Roma at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on April 05, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Napoli have had a rough start to the campaign, as the injury crisis from last season seems to have carried on with new problems into this.

Giovane also required an operation for a sports hernia, with Alessandro Buongiorno and Luca Marianucci already long-term absentees.

COMO, ITALY – MAY 02: Kevin De Bruyne of SSC Napoli looks on during the Serie A match between Como 1907 and SSC Napoli at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on May 02, 2026 in Como, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Kevin De Bruyne made good impacts off the bench in the first two games, but is not fully fit, so Antonio Vergara steps into a deeper midfield role.

Hojlund is again flanked by Alisson Santos and Matteo Politano.

Napoli are unbeaten against Inter since the Supercoppa Italiana Final in January 2024, managing one win and four draws.

NAPLES, ITALY – AUGUST 30: Massimiliano Allegri, Manager of Napoli, looks on during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Como 1907 at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on August 30, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

Inter: J Martinez; Bisseck, Akanji, Bastoni; Diouf, Barella, Zielinski, Sucic, Dimarco; Esposito, Lautaro Martinez

Napoli: Meret; Di Lorenzo, Rrahmani, Marin, Spinazzola; Anguissa, Lobotka, Vergara; Politano, Hojlund, Alisson Santos

articles.title: Fantasy Footballers’ Andy Holloway is a dedicated zero-inbox kinda guy
articles.summary: Andy Holloway, the cohost of the Fantasy Footballers podcast, keeps tabs to a minimum and doesn’t let email pile up.
articles.body: Andy Holloway cohosts the Fantasy Footballers podcast with his friends Jason Moore and Mike Wright. The show is one of the premier fantasy sports podcasts, netting over 2 million monthly listeners and numerous awards, including Best Sports Podcast from iHeartRadio and People’s Choice at the Podcast Awards four years in a row. Holloway’s goal has always been about bringing fantasy football to a wider audience, not just hardcore nerds. With the NFL season starting next week and fantasy drafts in full swing, now seemed like a great time to see how Holloway stays focused during what is probably the busiest part of the year for a serious fantasy football fan. What is one thing you wish you could change about your phone? I wish it was less intrusive in everyday life. No matter how much I customize things, I am still overwhelmed with notifications and messages and things that “seem” required. How many tabs do you have open right now? Just 2! I’m very much a tidy tab user and a zero-inbox type of guy. What is your favorite gadget you’ve ever owned? I truly love my Whoop! It helps me stay motivated and accountable, barely needs to be charged, and builds camaraderie with friends. I resisted for years, thinking it was dumb, but I love it. What creation are you most proud of? Certainly, building The Fantasy Footballers. People told us we couldn’t bootstrap it, but working with my best friends on a project we loved was the most satisfying accomplishment. What do you do when you need to focus? I try to knock out a ton of little things in a small period of time to feel like I’ve cleared a bunch of stuff off my list. It helps me stay focused on high-priority items without the noise of a bunch of small things hanging over me! What’s the last piece of physical media you bought? articles.title: Donna Mills does 100 sit-ups a day, plays tennis five times a week at 85 but won't quit Doritos
articles.summary: Donna Mills revealed her grueling daily fitness routine and confessed to a Doritos "addiction" she's carried through her decades-long career.
articles.body: Donna Mills is keeping fans on their toes at 85, from launching an OnlyFans account to revealing the intense fitness routine she credits with keeping her active. The former ballerina, best known for playing the scheming Abby Cunningham on "Knots Landing," revealed to Fox News Digital the demanding fitness routine she credits with keeping her moving — including 100 sit-ups, 50 leg lifts, up to an hour on the bike and, sometimes, tennis five days a week. And while Mills has long been disciplined about her health — including cutting out sugar — there is one indulgence she refuses to completely give up. 'KNOTS LANDING' STAR DONNA MILLS SAYS REFUSING TO POSE NUDE COST HER PLAYBOY COVER "I’m a Doritos addict," Mills confessed. The actress revealed that nacho cheese is her flavor of choice, showing that even her disciplined wellness routine leaves room for a guilty pleasure. "I mean, it’s not good for you. It’s not. You know, I know I shouldn’t do it," Mills admitted. WATCH: 'Knots Landing' star Donna Mills swears by this daily routine at 85 Still, she said the popular snack has followed her throughout her decades-long career. "Different sets that I’ve been on… for some reason, they know — they always got a bag of Doritos in the trailer for me… it’s really funny. But I’ve never lost that. I don’t eat them as much as I used to. But they’re still a treat." When it comes to exercise, Mills' routine is considerably more demanding. "I started out as a dancer, so a ballerina. I mean, I was on pointe, the whole thing," she said. 'KNOTS LANDING' STAR DONNA MILLS ISSUES URGENT WARNING ABOUT AGING Mills said her early training instilled a work ethic that has stuck with her throughout her life. "So that gave me a discipline that most people don’t have because ballet is very hard," she explained. To this day, she still incorporates elements of her early training into her workouts. DICK VAN DYKE SHOCKS FANS BY POSTING INVERSION TABLE WORKOUT AT AGE 100 "I do 100 sit-ups a day, 50 leg lifts, lots of stretching. I have a ballet barre in my little gym." Her rigorous routine doesn’t stop there. "And ride the bike for about 45 minutes or an hour," she continued. WATCH: Donna Mills says Playboy snubbed her over nude photo refusal She also stays active on the court whenever she can. "I play tennis five times a week sometimes. And so that’s very, very important." The Hollywood actress takes a similarly disciplined approach to her diet, saying a book she read years ago influenced her decision to cut back on sweets. "I’ve always been anti-sugar," she said. "I read a book a long time ago called 'Sugar Blues' that really talked about the sugar industry and everything, and I have stayed away from it ever since." Still, Mills isn't pretending her lifestyle is effortless. "It’s a lot of stuff. You got to work at it." 'PERFECT' WORKOUT FORMULA CAN TAKE JUST 10 MINUTES A DAY, HILARIA BALDWIN SAYS Her fitness routine comes as Mills enters what she describes as an entirely new chapter of her life. The actress launched an OnlyFans account at 85, embracing a platform she initially knew nothing about. But money isn't the only draw. Mills said fans are hungry for a behind-the-scenes look at her life — something she said wasn't possible during her TV heyday. "They want to know me. They want to know what I do during the day when I’m home. They want to see my home. They want to know much more about my personal life than we ever experienced back in the ’80s and the ’90s that, you know, the fans were cut off from." Now, they’re "invited in" — potentially even to Mills’ vineyard. Her OnlyFans audience has already made some unusual requests, including one involving barefoot grape-stomping. The decision also gave the Hollywood actress a chance to share never-before-seen photographs from a Playboy shoot that she says did not result in a promised cover. Mills said she agreed to the shoot only after making it clear she would not pose nude. "I said I would do the photo shoot for Playboy if they were okay with the fact that I wasn’t going to show anything," she recalled. But she said the photographer continued pushing her boundaries throughout the three-day shoot. Mills insisted the photos didn't need nudity to make an impression. "They’re very sexy," she exclaimed. That’s kind of always been my thing, to be a little spicy," Mills said. "I think they’ll react to that, they’ll like that, and also it’s my chance to communicate with them through the videos and things like that and talk to them." For Mills, the point isn't simply launching a provocative new platform. It's proving that getting older doesn't mean life gets smaller. "When I kind of looked at it a few years ago and said, 'What do I want to do with this portion of my life, this chapter in my life?' I said, 'I’d like to be an inspiration,'" she emphasized. articles.title: Dolly Parton’s sister slams ‘fake AI garbage’ flooding the internet since icon’s death
articles.summary: Dolly Parton’s sister has condemned the AI deepfakes circulating in the wake of the beloved American icon’s death.
articles.body: Dolly Parton’s sister has condemned the AI deepfakes circulating in the wake of the beloved American icon’s death. Stella Parton, 77, addressed the fake AI-generated images and videos being of her sister in a statement shared to Instagram Friday, where she also thanked fans for their “genuine” support. “Sadly, because of the way our lives have been lived in front of the public, we have no choice but to be subjected to incredible pressure and insensitivity from strangers,” she wrote. “There is a tremendous amount of AI and endless garbage being posted everyday and it’s been challenging to absorb and or ignore.” “As time passes, those who are in the business of exploiting the loss and tragedies of others on a daily basis will move on to the next stampede of endless misinformation,” she added. It marks Stella’s most extensive comments yet on the online reaction since the larger-than-life country singer died a little more than a week ago following a brief battle with cancer. She was 80. The younger Parton is a country singer and songwriter in her own right. Stella had several hit songs in the 1970s, including “I Want to Hold You in My Dreams Tonight,” which was released in 1975. She is one of the American icon’s 11 siblings. “We will be okay in time but each of us will grieve in our own personal way,” she wrote. “Every human being experiences pain and loss in life and my family is no different.” Stella Parton said that her “big sister Dolly would be surprised and delighted by the love her family and she has been shown during this time.” “She loved her fans and the public in general,” she wrote. “That is the reason she chose not to express her opinions on a lot of things like politics, religion and individuals in the public eye.” She asked fans to “show more compassion and wisdom as we move forward in life.” “Use my sister’s life as an example for tolerance and respect toward others,” she wrote. “It’s not about the most clever comments, fake AI garbage or snarky tweets.” “At the end of the day or the end of a life, how will you feel about yourself?”

images.caption: Stella Parton and Dolly Parton in Nashville in 2014.

articles.title: Miss America contestant reveals surprising day job as Massachusetts police officer
articles.summary: Ashlyn Mercier became the first police officer named Miss Massachusetts and now competes for the Miss America crown while serving her community.
articles.body: Ashlyn Mercier has spent her career wearing a badge. Now, she's hoping to wear one of the country's most coveted tiaras. The Westborough, Massachusetts, police officer is competing in Miss America. The final competition takes place Sept. 6 at the Palm Beach County Convention Center in West Palm Beach, Florida. Mercier is also the first police officer to be named Miss Massachusetts. "I think there's not one single look for what a female police officer is supposed to look like," Mercier told Fox News Digital. "And if we say that there is, that's just wrong because, at the end of the day, yes, female law enforcement officers only make up approximately 14% of the force in the United States, but we don't have to look a certain way." NAVY VETERAN TRADES MILITARY UNIFORM FOR MISS GEORGIA SASH FOLLOWING HEARTBREAKING LOSS "People are so multifaceted, women are so multifaceted, and I'm just trying to show young girls that they can chase all of their dreams simultaneously," Mercier said. "They don't have to pick one thing and make that their entire identity." The glitzy competition dates to a 1921 beauty contest in Atlantic City, New Jersey, held a year after the 19th Amendment guaranteed women the right to vote. The organization awards scholarships and gives its titleholder a national platform for community service and advocacy. Mercier hopes to raise awareness of her cause, "Nick's Courage: One Smile Goes a Mile," named after her younger brother, Nicholas, a two-time pediatric cancer survivor. The initiative aims to bring positivity and hope to children battling critical illnesses. In 2025, she took a year off from pageant competition to follow in her father's footsteps and attend the police academy. WATCH: ACTIVE-DUTY POLICE OFFICER COMPETES IN MISS AMERICA "I didn't know if I would ever come back and compete," Mercier said. "I was afraid of what other people would think if I chased both of those dreams at the same time. I also had this dream of becoming a police officer. But what I came to realize is that I can't worry about what other people think. I've got to focus on myself. And it ended up working out for me." Mercier said the Westborough Police Department has been cheering her on as she balances the competition with her work as an officer. Fox News Digital reached out to the department for comment. "I'm really fortunate that they have been so incredibly supportive," Mercier said. "I work for an amazing department, and my co-workers have supported me 100% from the moment I told them I was competing as Miss Massachusetts to now being at Miss America. They've shown up to my sendoff parties, they've helped me with my fundraising efforts, they've sent me good luck texts." "It's really just an honor to be surrounded by people who uplift me," she said. "It really continues to help motivate me to move forward." Mercier said her career in law enforcement doesn't give her an advantage on the Miss America stage. She's one of the delegates representing the 50 states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico, each hoping to stand out. Still, other officers have taken notice. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "I've had thousands of female law enforcement officers across the country commenting on my posts saying that they're rooting for me and that they're inspired by me," Mercier said. "There are also young girls saying that they want to get into law enforcement, and they're inspired by my story. And then, I serve my community in Westborough every single day in my capacity as a police officer, but I also get to serve my community in the role as Miss Massachusetts." "Those two things are what is so important about the Miss America opportunity," Mercier said. "Yes, we get to dress up. Yes, we get to wear pretty gowns and look beautiful. But, women's empowerment and service are the core. And if you look at it like that, you can see and draw a lot of parallels between Miss America and between my role as Officer Mercier." Police work has also given Mercier skills she can use in the competition. She said she's comfortable communicating with different people and staying calm in nerve-wracking situations. But one challenge remains. When asked whether getting ready for a shift or a pageant takes longer, she didn't miss a beat. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "Oh, absolutely getting ready for a pageant," she said with a laugh. "I do not look like this on a daily basis when I go to work. I'll have maybe some mascara on, and the hair gets slicked back in a bun. I've got that down in about two minutes flat. This definitely takes a lot longer." PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE This year's competition commemorates 105 years of Miss America. Whether she earns the title or not, Mercier said she's determined to use her platform to make a difference. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "If I do win, I just hope to be an inspiration to young women and girls looking up to [me] knowing that she can be a police officer, and she can be Miss America," Mercier said. "She can chase all her dreams at once. I've been told I should pick one, focus on one. But you can do it all. My message is to inspire the next generation."
